name: source-ref-episode-drift
definition: practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS (line 33: severity, window, what, where) decide every field update_registry() applies on a REVISED event (lines 230-234); source_ref -- set once, at NOTARIZED, from the observed record (line 213's `**record` spread) -- is not among them and is never reassigned again. For GDACS-sourced futures, source_ref is built (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py, gdacs_futures(), line 97) from the feed's own properties.url.report, a URL that embeds GDACS's current episodeid for that event and that GDACS changes every time it issues a new episode. stage/generate.py (lines 474-477) prints this exact field, unconditionally, as the only per-future outbound citation link on the public site ("the source's own report →"). obs-2026-09-18-1.json found 10 of the 92 OPEN GDACS futures where the episodeid embedded in the registry's stored source_ref no longer matches the episodeid GDACS's current feed reports for the same eventid -- from a 1-episode gap up to 32 (gdacs-tc-1001305: stored 15, current 47, six REVISED events since) -- and one control case, gdacs-fl-1104124, whose source_ref still matches only because its single REVISED event happened not to coincide with an episode-number change at GDACS.
test_rule: On each discovery pass, for every OPEN GDACS-sourced future in foreknown/registry.json with at least one REVISED event in its history: extract the episodeid query parameter from the future's stored source_ref (regex `episodeid=(\d+)`), and extract properties.episodeid from the same eventid's entry in the newest preserved foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json (matched on properties.eventid). If the two values differ, the sensor fires for that future, reporting the future id, the stored episode, the current episode, and the gap between them. No threshold or multiple-night wait is needed -- like sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json and sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json, this is a mechanical comparison against already-committed registry and snapshot bytes, and tonight's 10 confirmed instances are themselves the finding.
falsification: Falsified as a description of a live gap the moment either (a) update_registry() is changed to refresh source_ref whenever the underlying feed's own url.report/episodeid changes for an OPEN future -- whether by adding it to TRACKED_FIELDS or a parallel always-refreshed field -- and a future that is later revised again shows its citation link move with it, in which case the sensor should be retired as settled rather than kept firing against a fixed condition, or (b) the maintainer decides source_ref is intended to anchor a future permanently to the episode it was first notarized against (a historical citation, not a live one) and documents that choice, in which case this sensor should be retired as not-a-bug rather than promoted. Also falsified in scope for the one future class where it does not apply: NHC-sourced futures (source_ref a fixed https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/ constant, practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py line 121) and NWS-sourced futures (source_ref built from a CAP alert's own @id, line 212, which this observatory has not yet confirmed does or does not change on revision) carry no comparable per-episode GDACS URL structure, so this sensor is scoped to GDACS-sourced futures only -- the same scoping sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json and sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json already apply to other GDACS-only fields. Would also be falsified in substance, not merely in scope, if a wider sample showed GDACS's report.aspx page ignores its own episodeid query parameter and always serves the event's current episode regardless of the number in the URL -- untested by this observatory, which reads only the preserved feed JSON and does not fetch report.aspx pages.

promotion.settles: the proposal's own bar: a mechanical, stateless comparison against already-committed bytes, with no threshold or multiple-night wait named in its test_rule, whose 10 confirmed instances were already the finding the night it was written (obs-2026-09-18-1.json). Re-run tonight, a later night, against the same committed registry.json and the newest preserved foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-18/gdacs.json (no notary run had yet posted for 2026-09-19 at the time of this pass), the test_rule reproduces the identical 10 futures and gaps obs-2026-09-18-1.json reported, unchanged because the underlying committed record has not moved since: gdacs-tc-1001305 (15->47, gap 32), gdacs-fl-1104121 (2->14, gap 12), gdacs-fl-1104081 (7->18, gap 11), gdacs-tc-1001297 (51->55, gap 4), gdacs-dr-1018332 (18->21, gap 3), gdacs-dr-1018431 (11->14, gap 3), gdacs-dr-1027450 (5->8, gap 3), gdacs-dr-1027465 (2->5, gap 3), gdacs-dr-1027449 (6->8, gap 2), gdacs-wf-1030252 (39->40, gap 1).
implemented_in: practice/src/practice/foreknown/run.py, source_ref_drift field wired into run.json as source_ref_episode_drift
promotion.test_rule_held: verified by direct computation against foreknown/registry.json (current) and foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-18/gdacs.json: same 10 futures, same stored/current episode pairs and gaps obs-2026-09-18-1.json first reported. The function is unit-tested against fixed fixtures (drift, no-drift, and the unrevised/closed/non-GDACS exclusions the definition and falsification clause both name) rather than only against tonight's live data, so the check keeps firing correctly once the underlying record does move.
promotion.kept_unchanged: definition, test_rule and falsification are the machine's text from 2026-09-18 and match the code as written: episodeid/eventid read from source_ref by the same regex shape the test_rule specifies, matched against the newest preserved GDACS snapshot's properties.eventid, scoped to OPEN GDACS futures with at least one REVISED event, no threshold added. Neither falsification condition has occurred -- update_registry()'s TRACKED_FIELDS (futures.py) still does not include source_ref, and no maintainer note declares source_ref a permanent, first-episode anchor -- so the gap this sensor watches for is still open, which is why it is promoted running as-is rather than retired.
